title: 过 (guo) in Chinese: HSK 2 Grammar with Examples
description: How to use 过 (guo) to say you have done something before: word order, negatives with 没有, questions, 过 vs 了, and 13 HSK 2 example sentences.
h1: How to Use 过 (guo) for Past Experience
lede: 过 (guo) goes after a verb to say that you have done something at some time in the past: you have been to China, you have eaten dumplings, you have met someone. It is a key grammar point of HSK 2.

paras: Put 过 straight after the verb. It is said with a neutral tone (guo). The sentence tells you that this has happened at least once in your life, but not exactly when. In English this is usually "have done" or "have ever done".
To say you have never done something, put 没有 before the verb and keep 过. This is different from 了, which you drop in a negative sentence.
The most common mistake is to use 不. 我不去过中国 is wrong: 过 is always negated with 没有, never with 不.

examples.py: Tā méiyǒu kàn guo zhège diànyǐng.
examples.en: He has never seen this film.

examples.py: Wǒ māma méiyǒu hē guo kāfēi.
examples.en: My mum has never had coffee.

paras: Add 吗 at the end, or end the question with 没有. To answer yes, repeat the verb with 过, as in 去过. To answer no, say 没有, or 没有 with the verb and 过, as in 没有去过.

examples.py: Nǐ chī guo Zhōngguó cài ma?
examples.en: Have you ever had Chinese food?
Have you ever been on a plane?

paras: 了 tells you that one action happened or that something has changed. 过 tells you about an experience. 他去中国了 means he has gone to China and is probably there now. 他去过中国 means he has been there at some point and is not there any more.
You can add a time word or a number of times to a 过 sentence when you want to say a little more about the experience.

examples.en: He has gone to China (he's there now).
He has been to China (and is back now).

examples.py: Tā qùnián qù guo yí cì Zhōngguó.
examples.en: He went to China once last year.

sections.h2: 过 goes right after the verb
paras: 过 never goes at the end after the object. Say 我学过汉语, not 我学汉语过. With verb-object words such as 见面, 过 goes between the two parts: 见过面.

examples.py: Wǒmen hái méiyǒu jiàn guo miàn.

worksheet.title: 过 (guo) Worksheet: HSK 2 Printable with Answers
worksheet.description: A free printable 过 (guo) worksheet for HSK 2: 20 exercises (过 or 了, word order, fix the mistake) with an answer key.

exercises.instructions: Write 过 or 了 in each gap. The English tells you what the sentence means.

items.en: Have you ever eaten dumplings?
I've never been to his home.
It's started raining, let's go home.
I have met his mum before.
He has already gone to bed.
Have you ever seen this film?
It's got hot.
I've never been on a plane.
I'm eighteen now.

exercises.instructions: Write the words as one correct sentence with 过.

items.en: I've been on a train before.
He has never studied Chinese.
Have you ever had Chinese tea?
We've been to this restaurant before.
I've never read this book.
She has worked in China.

exercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Write the correct sentence.

items.en: I've never been to that shop.
He has never had dumplings.
She has never had coffee.
I have studied Chinese before.
She has never been to my home.
